question: Should OpenClaw adopt the public `api.registerReadinessCriterion` Plugin SDK contract and ship the `local`, `container`, `reverse-proxy`, and `node-mode` profiles as supported readiness behavior in V1?
rationale: This PR changes durable plugin, configuration, CLI, readiness, and host-probe contracts; code review cannot decide whether that permanent product and compatibility surface is desired.

options.title: Approve the V1 contract and profile set
options.body: Treat the Plugin SDK registration API and four opt-in profiles as supported surfaces, then require the exact-head Docker conformance matrix before merge.

options.title: Land core readiness first
options.body: Defer profiles and plugin registration until maintainers have accepted the narrower core readiness contract and its upgrade boundary.

options.title: Decline built-in profiles
options.body: Keep readiness directly configurable and route any deployment-specific posture bundle to a plugin or external deployment documentation.

recommendation.title: Approve the V1 contract and profile set
recommendation.body: Treat the Plugin SDK registration API and four opt-in profiles as supported surfaces, then require the exact-head Docker conformance matrix before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the linked RFC and the coordinated readiness/profile stack, making them the best available contact to clarify the design; final acceptance requires a core maintainer.
